[[Switch Mobility]]}} | website = {{URL|http://www.ashokleyland.com}} | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1948|09|07}} | hq_location = [[Chennai]], [[Tamil Nadu]], India }} '''Ashok Leyland Limited''' is an Indian [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[automotive]] manufacturer headquartered in [[Chennai]] and owned by the [[Hinduja Group]].{{cite news|title=Who are the Hinduja brothers|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news/who-sri-gopi-hinduja-brothers-10372393|access-date=8 May 2017|publisher=The Mirror|date=7 May 2017|last=O'Leary|first=Abigail}} Founded in 1948 as Ashok Motors, it as renamed Ashok Leyland in 1955 following a collaboration with [[British Leyland]].{{Cite news |last=Moneycontrol.com |title=Ashok Leyland > Company History > Auto - LCVs & HCVs > Company History of Ashok Leyland - BSE: 500477, NSE: ASHOKLEY |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/company-facts/ashokleyland/history/AL |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220414152325/https://www.moneycontrol.com/company-facts/ashokleyland/history/AL |archive-date=2022-04-14 |access-date=2026-01-29 |language=en}} Today it is the second-largest manufacturer of commercial vehicles in India (holding a 32.1% market share as of 2016), the third-largest bus manufacturer,{{Cite news |date=2020-02-04 |title=How Ashok Leyland became world’s third largest bus manufacturer |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/auto/car-news/ashok-leyland-worlds-third-largest-bus-manufacturer-electric-buses-ashok-leyland-sales-2019/1855250/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125140017/https://www.financialexpress.com/auto/car-news/ashok-leyland-worlds-third-largest-bus-manufacturer-electric-buses-ashok-leyland-sales-2019/1855250/ |archive-date=2020-11-25 |access-date=2026-01-29 |work=The Financial Express |language=en-US}} and the tenth-largest manufacturer of lorries. While its corporate office is located in [[Chennai]], the company operates manufacturing facilities in [[Ennore]], [[Bhandara (city)|Bhandara]], [[Vijayawada]], [[Hosur]], [[Alwar]], and [[Pantnagar]].{{Cite web |last=Pradesh |first=Andhra |date=2025-03-20 |title='Ashok Leyland Plant launch marks new era': Minister Nara Lokesh |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/andhra-pradesh/2025/Mar/20/ashok-leyland-plant-launch-marks-new-era-minister-nara-lokesh |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Ashok Leyland Ltd India, Map of Ashok Leyland Motor Plants|url=https://business.mapsofindia.com/commercial-vehicles-industry/ashok-leyland.html|access-date=2020-10-15|website=business.mapsofindia.com}}{{Cite web|title=Ashok Leyland Pantnagar {{!}} Perkins|url=https://www.perkins.com/en_GB/products/sectors/electric-power/ep-case-studies/ashok-leyland-pantnagar.html|access-date=2020-10-15|website=perkins.com}} Ashok Leyland also has overseas manufacturing units in [[Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates|Ras Al Khaimah]], United Arab Emirates, and [[Leeds]], United Kingdom. Additionally, it has a joint venture with the Alteams Group to manufacture high-press die-casting extruded [[aluminium]] components for the automotive and telecommunications sectors.{{Cite news|title=Ashok Leyland Ltd.|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/ashok-leyland-31/information/company-history|access-date=2020-10-15}} The company also makes spare parts and engines for industrial and marine applications. Ashok Leyland's products range from 1-tonne Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) to 55-tonne Gross Trailer Weight (GTW). This includes trucks, buses ranging from 9 to 80 seats, vehicles for defence and special applications, and diesel engines for industrial, genset, and marine applications.{{Cite web|title=About Us |website=Ashok Leyland |url=https://www.ashokleyland.com/en/about-us |access-date=2020-10-15}} In 2019, the company claimed to be ranked in the top 10 global commercial vehicle makers.{{Cite news|title=Ashok Leyland eyes top 10 CV slot with organisational rejig|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/auto-news/ashok-leyland-rings-in-top-order-organisational-change/articleshow/69890798.cms|access-date=2020-10-15}} It sold approximately 140,000 vehicles (M&HCV and LCV) in 2016. The company has passenger transportation options ranging from 10 seaters to 74 seaters (M&HCV = LCV). In the trucks segment, Ashok Leyland primarily concentrates on the 16 to 25-tonne range and has a presence in the 7.5 to 49 tonne range. {{Multiple image|perrow = 2|total_width=375|align=right |image1 = EXCON 2025, Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (329).jpg |width1 = 125px |image2 = EXCON 2025, Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (777).jpg |width2 = 125px |footer = Ashok Leyland at [[EXCON]] 2025, [[Bangalore International Exhibition Centre|BIEC]] }} ==History== [[File:Ashok Leyland 2018 stampsheet of India.jpg|thumb|A 2018 stamp sheet of India dedicated to the 70th anniversary of Ashok Leyland]] ===Ashok Motors=== Ashok Motors was founded in 1948 by [[Raghunandan Saran]], an [[Indian independence movement|Indian independence]] campaigner from [[Punjab, India|Punjab]].{{cite news |url=http://www.hindu.com/mp/2008/09/01/stories/2008090150830800.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080922095548/http://www.hindu.com/mp/2008/09/01/stories/2008090150830800.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 September 2008|title=Ashok Leyland-A pioneer's Diamond Jubilee|date=1 September 2008 |access-date=15 February 2014 |work=[[The Hindu]]|location=Chennai, India}} By the end of the [[Indian independence movement|Indian Independence Movement]], he was persuaded by India's first Prime Minister [[Jawaharlal Nehru]] to invest in a modern industrial venture. Ashok Motors was incorporated in 1948 as a company to assemble and manufacture [[Austin Motor Company|Austin]] cars from [[England]], and the company was named after the founder's only son, Ashok Saran. The company had its headquarters in [[Chennai]], with the manufacturing plant also in Chennai. The company was engaged in the assembly and distribution of [[Austin A40]] passenger cars in India.{{fact|date=September 2023}} In year 1954 Indian government gave approvals to Ashok Motors to manufacturer [[Leyland Comet]] trucks the generation range of [[Cab over|cabover]] trucks from Leyland and they also received approvals to manufacture [[Leyland Tiger Cub|Tiger Cub]] lightweight bus also by Leyland. These were the first models of British Leyland manufactured in india.{{Cite web |title=LEYLANDS TO BE BUILT IN INDIA {{!}} 7th May 1954 {{!}} The Commercial Motor Archive |url=https://archive.commercialmotor.com/article/7th-may-1954/46/leylands-to-be-built-in-india |access-date=2023-04-28 |website=archive.commercialmotor.com}} The collaboration ended in 1975 but the holding of [[British Leyland]], which was then a major British vehicle conglomerate due to several mergers, agreed to assist in technology, which continued until the 1980s. After 1975, changes in management structures saw the company launch various vehicles in the Indian market, with many of these models continuing to this day with various upgrades. ===Under Iveco and Hinduja partnership=== In 1987, the overseas holding by Land Rover Leyland International Holdings Limited (LRLIH) was taken over by a joint venture between the Hinduja Group, the Non-Resident Indian transnational group and [[Iveco]], part of the [[Fiat Chrysler Automobiles|Fiat Group]].[http://archive.commercialmotor.com/article/20th-august-1987/16/rover-to-quit-ashok Rover to quit Ashtok] ''[[Commercial Motor]]'' 20 August 1987 page 16 ===Hinduja Group=== In 2007, the Hinduja Group bought out Iveco's indirect stake in Ashok Leyland.{{Cite web |date=25 July 2006 |title=Hindujas buy out Iveco's 15% stake in Leyland |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/hindujas-buy-out-ivecos-15-stake-in-leyland/articleshow/1802931.cms |access-date=2022-05-02 |website=The Times of India |language=en}} The promoter shareholding now stands at 51%. Today the company is the flagship of the [[Hinduja Group]], a British-based and Indian originated trans-national [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]]. The plant will produce 2,500 vehicles a year, initially, and will gradually increase to 5,000 per year in the next decade. This facility will mainly produce electric buses. The plant will be launched in 2025.{{Cite news |last=Saxena |first=Ragini |date=2024-03-07 |title=Tata & Ashok Leyland get busy on a bumpy road to India's green transport push |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/tata-ashok-leyland-get-busy-on-a-bumpy-road-to-indias-green-transport-push/articleshow/108287847.cms |access-date=2024-03-08 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} ==Partnerships== ===Rosoboronexport & ELCOM=== Ashok Leyland Defence Systems (ALDS), Russia's [[Rosoboronexport]] and ELCOM Group have signed a cooperation agreement in defence business to provide tracked vehicles to the [[Indian Armed Forces]]. The agreement was signed on the side lines of the 2017 International Military Technical Forum Army held at [[Kubinka]], near [[Moscow]], on 25 August 2017.{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/ashok-leyland-arm-russian-company-defence-pact-elcom/article9848412.ece|title=Ashok Leyland arm, ELCOM ink defence pact with Russian firm|date=6 September 2017 |access-date=31 July 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.hino-global.com/news_release/255.html|title=Hino Motors and Ashok Leyland have entered into a Mutual Cooperation Agreement – NEWS RELEASE LIST |website= Hino Global |access-date=31 July 2018}} ===IIT Madras=== Ashok Leyland and [[Indian Institute of Technology Madras]] (IIT Madras) signed a memorandum of understanding, on 19 August 2017, for Ashok Leyland to sponsor the Centre of Battery Engineering (CoBE) at IIT Madras. As part of the agreement, Ashok Leyland partnered with IIT Madras to carry out research and development (R&D) activities for strengthening battery engineering and related sub-parts, especially for electric vehicles.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ashokleyland.com/|title=Ashok Leyland | Commercial Vehicles, Buses, Trucks & Mobility Solutions|website=www.ashokleyland.com}}{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ashok-leyland-signs-mou-with-iit-madras-to-carry-r-d-activities-on-battery-engineering-for-ev-117082200455_1.html|title=Ashok Leyland and IIT Madras to research battery tech for electric vehicles|first=T. E.|last=Narasimhan|newspaper=Business Standard India|date=22 August 2017|access-date=31 July 2018|via=Business Standard}} ===Sun Mobility=== On 18 July 2017 Ashok Leyland announced the formation of an alliance with [[SUN Mobility]], The global partnership aims to develop [[Electric vehicle|electric vehicles]]. === CVRDE partnership === [[File:CVRDE_600_HP_engine.jpg|thumb|CVRDE 600-hp engine.]] As reported in December 2021, Ashok Leyland has partnered with [[Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment]] (CVRDE) under the [[DRDO]] to design, develop and produce a 600-hp indigenous engine for the [[TATA Kestrel|DRDO WhAP]]. As per the reports the prototype engine has been manufactured and will undergo rigorous testing in the lab and will be qualified for application in [[Armoured fighting vehicle|armoured fighting vehicles]] (AFV). Series production is scheduled to begin after operational start-up. The testing was inaugurated in the Engine Development Centre, Ashok Leyland, Vellivoyalchavadi, near [[Chennai]].{{Cite press release |title=Development of 600 HP Engine under Self Reliant India (Atmanirbhar Bharat) |date=2021-12-15 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1782003 |access-date=2025-07-28}}{{Cite web |last= |date=2021-12-15 |title=Ashok Leyland partners with CVRDE to develop 600hp engine - ET Auto |url=https://auto.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/auto-components/ashok-leyland-partners-with-cvrde-to-develop-600hp-engine/88300699 |access-date=2024-11-01 |website=ETAuto.com |language=en}} ===Iveco partnership=== In the late 1980s, Iveco investment and partnership resulted in Ashok Leyland launching the 'Cargo' range of trucks based on European [[Ford Cargo]] trucks. The Cargo entered production in 1994, at Ashok Leyland's new plant in [[Hosur]].{{cite web|url=http://ashokleyland.com/historytxt.html|title=History: We cut our teeth on cars|publisher=Ashok Leyland|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011014031903/http://ashokleyland.com/hisbot.html|archive-date=14 October 2001}} These vehicles used Iveco engines and for the first time had factory-fitted cabs. Though the Cargo trucks are no longer in production and the use of Iveco engine was discontinued, the cab continues to be used on the Ecomet range of trucks as well as for several of Ashok Leyland's military vehicles. The Cargo was originally introduced in {{convert|7|and|9|LT|kg|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} versions; later, heavier-duty models from {{convert|15|to|26|LT|kg|sigfig=3|abbr=on}} were progressively introduced.{{cite web|url=http://ashokleyland.com/prodcargomain.html|title=Products: Cargo|publisher=Ashok Leyland|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011120081944/http://ashokleyland.com/prodcargomain.html|archive-date=20 November 2001}} ===ETG Group=== On 26 May 2022, Ashok Leyland has announced partnership with ETG Group to strengthen its partnership in Africa. As part of the tie-up, ETG Logistics (ETGL) will operate dealerships for Ashok Leyland in six key southern African countries.{{Cite news |title=Ashok Leyland partners with ETG Group to strengthen presence in Africa |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/auto-news/ashok-leyland-partners-with-etg-group-to-strengthen-presence-in-africa/articleshow/91813049.cms |access-date=2022-06-10}} ===South Indian Bank=== Ashok Leyland and [[South Indian Bank]] signed a memorandum of understanding, on 18 April 2024, for providing competitive finance options to the dealers of the truck and bus maker. As part of the agreement, South Indian Bank will offer appropriate inventory financing solutions to Ashok Leyland's network of dealers.{{Cite news |agency=Press Trust of India|date=2024-04-18|title=Ashok Leyland, South Indian Bank sign MoU to provide financing to dealers |work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/ashok-leyland-south-indian-bank-sign-mou-to-provide-financing-to-dealers-124041800401_1.html |access-date=2024-04-18}} ==Products== File:Ashok Leyland Ecomet 912.jpg|Current generation Ashok Leyland eComet File:Karnataka Sarige BSVI ashok leyland bus.png|KSRTC'S Sarige bus File:BEST Bus Mumbai.jpg|Ashok Leyland Titan Double Decker bus of BEST, Mumbai File:Nmmtabc.jpg|Ashok Leyland City Transit Bus in Navi Mumbai File:Deluxe A.jpg|Ashok Leyland Inter-City Deluxe Bus operated by APSRTC File:India Trip 2009.jpg|Ashok Leyland Tusker Twin Axle Lorry with custom built cabin, a regular sight on Indian highways File:A lorry in Tamil Nadu.JPG|A 1980s-built short haul Ashok Leyland lorry in Tamil Nadu, still in operation File:City Bus Hyd.jpg|A Telangana State Road Transport Corporation TSRTC city bus in Hyderabad File:Ashok Leyland Tipper Truck 726.jpg|Ashok Leyland Comet [[dump truck|tipper lorry]] File:Ashok Leyland Arica.jpg|Ashok Leyland Eagle 814 in [[Arica]], [[Chile]] File:Iraqi Ashok Leyland truck.jpg|Ashok Leyland 1518, a rebadged [[Ford Cargo]] used by the Iraqi 2nd Brigade and [[7th Division (Iraq)|7th Iraqi Army Division]] at the Iraqi School of Infantry on Camp Yassir, Iraq. === Trucks === '''Current range''' *'''General''' * 1916 4x2 * 1920 4x2 *'''Boss''' Boss is an intermediate commercial vehicle launched by Ashok Leyland. The presently available models are: * 1115 * 1215 * 1315 * 1415 * 1920 *'''Ecomet''' * 1015 * 1115 * 1215 * 1415 * 1615 *'''AVTR Modular Platform''' * 1920 * 2620 (Life Axle Technology){{Cite news |title=Ashok Leyland unveils eight-wheel truck AVTR 2620 |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/lcv-hcv/ashok-leyland-unveils-eight-wheel-truck-avtr-2620/articleshow/91961200.cms |access-date=2022-06-10}} * 2620 6x2 (Single-Tire Lift Axle) * 2820 6x2 * 2820 6x4 * 2825 * 3120 6x2 (Double-Tire Lift Axle) * 3520 8x2 (Single-Tire Lift Axle/Twin Steer) * 3525 8x4 * 4020 * 4120 8x2 (Double-Tire Lift Axle) * 4125 8x2 (Double-Tire Lift Axle) * 4220 10x2 * 4225 10x2 * 4620 * 4825 10x2 (Double-Tire Lift Axle) * 4825 10x4 (Double-Tire Lift Axle) * 5225 * 5425 * 5525 4x2 * 5525 6x4 '''Former range''' * Beaver * Rhino * U-Truck * Captain ===Light Vehicles=== '''Current range''' * '''Dost''' * '''Bada Dost''' The Dost is a 1.25 ton light commercial vehicle (LCV) that is the first product to be launched by the Indian-Japanese commercial vehicle joint venture Ashok Leyland Nissan Vehicles. Dost is powered by a 58 hp high-torque, 3-cylinder, turbo-charged common rail diesel engine and has a payload capacity of 1.25 tonnes. It is available in both BS3 and BS4 versions. The bodywork and some of the underpinnings relate to Nissan's [[Nissan Vanette#Second generation (C22; 1985–1994)|C22 Vanette]] of the 1980s; this is most visible in the door design. The LCV is produced in Ashok Leyland's Hosur plant in Tamil Nadu. The LCV is available in three versions. With the launch of Dost Ashok Leyland has now entered the Light Commercial Vehicle segment in India{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/article1582657.ece|title=Ashok Leyland enters LCV segment with Dost|publisher=The Hindu Business Line|access-date=29 May 2012}}{{cite web|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/news/ashok-leyland-dost-rolled-out/768748/2|title=Ashok Leyland DOST' rolled out|date=29 March 2011|publisher=Financialexpress.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029203050/http://www.financialexpress.com/news/ashok-leyland-dost-rolled-out/768748/2|archive-date=29 October 2013|url-status=dead|access-date=29 May 2012}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.overdrive.in:80/story-news-general_news/ashok_leyland_dost_unveiled-40372-0.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720083938/http://www.overdrive.in/story-news-general_news/ashok_leyland_dost_unveiled-40372-0.html|url-status=dead|title=Ashok Leyland Dost unveiled - New Ashok Leyland LCV - News : Overdrive|archivedate=20 July 2011|website=www.overdrive.in}}{{cite news|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-03-29/news/29357827_1_andy-palmer-ashok-leyland-nissan-jv-lcvs|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515222534/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-03-29/news/29357827_1_andy-palmer-ashok-leyland-nissan-jv-lcvs|url-status=dead|archive-date=15 May 2012|title=Ashok Leyland-Nissan JV unveil first LCV model- Dost, targets below 3 tonne market|date=29 March 2011|access-date=29 May 2012|publisher=Articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com}} * '''STiLE''' [[File:Ashok_Leyland_STiLE.jpg|thumb|200px|Ashok Leyland STiLE light commercial vehicle]] [[Ashok Leyland STiLE|STiLE]] is a [[multi-purpose vehicle]] which was manufactured by Ashok Leyland. The vehicle was unveiled during the 2012 [[Auto Expo]] and was launched in July 2013. STiLE was marketed as a "multi-purpose vehicle" for use as a hotel shuttle, [[taxi]], [[ambulance]], and [[panel van]], and in [[courier]] service. In May 2015, Ashok Leyland stopped production due to low demand.{{cite news|title=Ashok Leyland introduces STiLE|publisher=[[Business Standard]]|access-date=31 July 2018|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cd/ashok-leyland-introduces-the-stile-113071601035_1.html}}{{cite news|title=Ashok Leyland discontinues STiLE|publisher=[[NDTV]]|access-date=31 July 2018|url=https://www.carandbike.com/news/ashok-leyland-discontinues-the-stile-mpv-in-india-762700}}{{cite news|title=STiLE features|publisher=Ashok Leyland website|access-date=31 July 2018|url=http://www.ashokleylandlcv.com/stile-features|archive-date=27 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180327182402/http://www.ashokleylandlcv.com/stile-features|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=STiLE variants|publisher=Ashok Leyland website|access-date=31 July 2018|url=http://www.ashokleylandlcv.com/stile%E2%80%93variants|archive-date=18 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181118162520/http://ashokleylandlcv.com/stile%E2%80%93variants|url-status=dead}} '''Diesel Generators''' Ashok Leyland offers Diesel Generators manufactured with Ashok Leyland engines and Leypower alternators. Currently they manufacture 5 to 2250 kVA Silent DG Sets. ==Subsidiary ventures== ===Construction equipment=== In June 2009 the company expanded into construction equipment segment, with a 50:50 joint venture with [[John Deere]]. It was floated as a separate entity under the name of Leyland – Deere Limited.{{cite news|url=http://www.hindu.com/2009/07/15/stories/2009071550661400.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090719072320/http://www.hindu.com/2009/07/15/stories/2009071550661400.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 July 2009 |title=Leyland, John Deere complete JV formalities |date=15 July 2009 |access-date=29 May 2012 |work=[[The Hindu]] |location=Chennai, India}} ===Ashok Leyland Defence Systems=== [[File:Vehicle Factory Jabalpur (VFJ)'s Stallion Truck for the Indian Army.jpg|thumb|[[Vehicle Factory Jabalpur|Vehicle Factory Jabalpur (VFJ)]]'s Stallion 4X4 Truck for the Indian Army]] [[File:Agni-II missile (Republic Day Parade 2004).jpeg|thumb|An Indian road-mobile launcher with a ballistic missile]] [[File:STALLION KAVACH.JPG|thumb|Ashok Leyland's Stallion Kavach 4X4 Mine Protection Armoured Vehicle]] [[File:Pralay_missile_-_Indian_Republic_day_Parade_Rehearsal_2025.jpg|thumb|[[Pralay (missile)|Pralay missiles]] on Ashok Leyland [[Twelve wheel drive|12×12]] high mobility vehicle.]] [[Ashok Leyland Defence Systems]] (ALDS) is a newly floated company by the Hinduja Group. Ashok Leyland holds 26 percent in Ashok Leyland Defence Systems (ALDS). The company designs and develops defence logistics and tactical vehicles, defence communication and other systems.http://www.financialexpress.com/news/ashok-leyland-defence-arm-ties-up-with-kraussmaffei/753566/1 [https://web.archive.org/web/20110721192648/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-01-11/news/28427239_1_defence-business-defence-sector-defence-equipment], Ashok Leyland Defence Systems Ashok Leyland is the largest supplier of logistics vehicles to the Indian Army. It has supplied over 60,000 of its [[Ashok Leyland Stallion|Stallion]] vehicles, all manufactured at the [[Vehicle Factory Jabalpur|Vehicle Factory Jabalpur (VFJ)]].Ashok Leyland largest supplier of logistics vehicles to Indian Army. Over 60,000 Stallions.{{cite web|url=http://www.indiandefence.com/forums/f32/ashok-leyland-defence-kmw-develop-advanced-defence-systems-4664/ |title=Ashok Leyland Defence and KMW to develop advanced defence systems |access-date=11 March 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713025001/http://www.indiandefence.com/forums/f32/ashok-leyland-defence-kmw-develop-advanced-defence-systems-4664/ |archive-date=13 July 2011 }} ==International operations and exports== [[File:Ashok Leyland 3518iL Tractor New 2014.JPG|thumb|A new Ashok Leyland 3518iL chassis unit for custom built cab and load body]] Exports of commercial vehicles contribute to a seven percent share of Ashok Leyland's total revenues.{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/Ashok-Leyland-to-focus-on-exports/article14503111.ece|title=Ashok Leyland to focus on exports|first=N.|last=Anand|newspaper=The Hindu|date=23 July 2016|access-date=31 July 2018|via=www.thehindu.com}} The company has a presence in SAARC countries like Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal, and in the Middle East countries where it exports 3600–4000 units a year.{{cite web|url=http://autopartsasia.in/2016/09/26/ashok-leyland-explores-export-markets-new-products/|title=Ashok Leyland Explores Export Markets With New Products – Auto Parts Asia|date=26 September 2016|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180731213102/https://autopartsasia.in/2016/09/26/ashok-leyland-explores-export-markets-new-products/|archive-date=31 July 2018|url-status=dead}} The company has an assembly unit, mainly for buses, in Ras Al Khaimah in UAE to cater to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states.{{cite web|url=http://www.mydigitalfc.com/news/ashok-leyland-eyes-global-expansion-503|title=- mydigitalfc|website=mydigitalfc.com|access-date=31 July 2018}} This unit currently assembles 4000 units, which the company plans to increase to 6000 units. Ashok Leyland exports medium and heavy commercial vehicles to Arab countries like Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE and Yemen; former [[Soviet Union]] countries like Azerbaijan, Armenia, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Ukraine; Sub-Saharan Africa; Sri Lanka; Bangladesh; Nepal; the Philippines; Thailand and Malaysia. Every year Ashok Leyland exports about 12000 trucks to Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.{{Cite news |last=Barry |first=Cross |date=28 November 2017 |title=First shipments of trucks by sea from India to Bangladesh |pages=1 |work=Automotive Logistics |url=https://www.automotivelogistics.media/first-shipments-of-trucks-by-sea-from-india-to-bangladesh/19708.article }} On 11 June 2012, Ashok Leyland supplied 100 Falcon buses to Ghana for $7.6 million (about {{INR}}42 [[crore]]).{{cite news| url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/article3514562.ece | title=Ashok Leyland supplies 100 buses to Ghana for $7.6 million | date=11 June 2012}} Ashok Leyland was awarded the first overseas order worth $6 million for its vestibule buses from [[Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation]] (BRTC).{{cite news| url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Ashok-Leyland-bags-first-overseas-order-for-vestibule-buses/articleshow/13865526.cms | title=Ashok Leyland bags first overseas order for vestibule buses | date=6 June 2012 | work=The Times Of India}} ===Lanka Ashok Leyland=== [[File:LANKA ASHOK LEYLAND BUS OPERATED BY JANADHI TRAVELS AT BENTOTA BUS STATION BOUND FOR GALLE SRI LANKA JAN 2013 (8580307998).jpg|thumb|A Lanka Ashok Leyland bus in Sri Lanka in 2013]] [[Lanka Ashok Leyland]] (LAL) in [[Sri Lanka]] was formed in 1982 and started its operations in 1983 as a joint venture between Lanka Leyland Ltd (a wholly owned company of the Government of Sri Lanka) and Ashok Leyland Ltd India. LAL imports commercial vehicles in both knock down kits and fully built, and carries out assembly operations, repair and service, and body building on chassis.[http://www.lal.lk/ Welcome to Lanka Ashok Leyland]. Lal.lk. Retrieved on 16 July 2013. ===Switch Mobility=== [[File:Blazefield Starship Versa.jpg|thumb|An [[Optare Versa]] parked outside [[Optare]]'s [[Sherburn-in-Elmet]] factory]] In 2010 Ashok Leyland acquired a 26% stake in the British bus manufacturer Optare,[http://www.automotiveworld.com/analysis/83128-india-uk-ashok-leyland-takes-26-stake-in-optare/ Ashtok Leyland takes 26% stake in Optare] ''Automotive World'' 30 July 2010 a company that was originally based on the premises of a former British Leyland subsidiary [[Charles H Roe]] before moving to the new purpose-built factory in 2011 in [[Sherburn-in-Elmet]].[http://www.transportnewsbrief.co.uk/bus-and-coach/optares-efficient-new-uk-bus-production-plant/ Optare's efficient new UK bus production plant] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141202194147/http://www.transportnewsbrief.co.uk/bus-and-coach/optares-efficient-new-uk-bus-production-plant/ |date=2 December 2014 }} ''Transport News Brief'' 16 December 2013 In 2017, Ashok Leyland acquired a further 72.31% stake in Optare increasing its overall stake to 98.31%.{{cite web|url=http://www.optare.com/news/2017/12/1/ashok-leyland-increases-stake-in-optare|title=Ashok Leyland increases stake in Optare|date=December 2017|access-date=31 July 2018}}In 2018, the stake was further raised to 99.08%.{{Cite web |date=2018-10-26 |title=Ashok Leyland ups shareholding in Optare to 99.08% to help arm slash debt burden |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-ashok-leyland-ups-shareholding-in-optare-to-99-08-to-help-arm-slash-debt-burden-1361615/ |access-date=2025-03-18 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}} In November 2020, Ashok Leyland announced that Optare would be rebranded as [[Switch Mobility]].{{Cite web |last=WebSupport |date=2020-12-01 |title=Optare becomes Switch Mobility as parent company Ashok Leyland unveils global electric vehicle plans |url=https://cbwmagazine.com/optare-becomes-switch-mobility-as-parent-company-ashok-leyland-unveils-global-electric-vehicle-plans/ |access-date=2025-03-18 |website=CBW |language=en-GB}} ==Technology== ===Hythane engines=== Ashok Leyland has also developed [[hythane]] engines in association with the Australian company Eden Energy. Ashok Leyland developed a 6-cylinder, {{convert|6|L|cuin|adj=on}} {{convert|92|kW|hp|abbr=on}} BS-4 engine which uses hythane (H-CNG,) which is a blend of natural gas and around 20% of hydrogen. A 4-cylinder {{convert|4|L|cuin|adj=on}} {{convert|63|kW|hp|abbr=on}} engine is also being developed for H-CNG blend in a joint R&D program with MNRE (Ministry of New and Renewable Energy) and Indian Oil Corporation.{{Cite news |last=india |first=motor |date=2 April 2009 |title=Ashok Leyland develops hythane engines |pages=1 |work=Motorindia |url=https://www.motorindiaonline.in/ashok-leyland-develops-hythane-engines/ }} ===Hybrid technology=== ====Non-plugin Hybrid Bus==== At the Delhi Auto Expo 2016, Ashok Leyland introduced an advanced non-plug-in version of HYBUS. This model is powered by an H-Series 6-cylinder diesel engine (BS IV compliant), which is not used to drive the vehicle forward but to charge the ultra-capacitors that power the 150 kW electric motor. An automatic start-stop system is employed to reduce overall engine idling time. The bus can restart using the stored energy when the engine is off, enhancing fuel efficiency and decreasing NVH (noise, vibration, and harshness) levels.{{cite web|url=http://wagenclub.com/2016/02/ashok-leyland-hybus-hybrid-bus-tech-spec-review.html|title=Ashok Leyland HYBUS Hybrid Bus – 2016 Auto Expo – WagenClub|date=6 February 2016|access-date=31 July 2018}} ===Electric Technology=== In 2016 the company launched the country's first indigenously produced fully electric bus, called Circuit. The bus is a zero-emission vehicle that can run 120 km on a single charge, and has an alert system that can signal if the bus is low on power.{{cite web|url=http://commercialvehicle.in/circuit-from-ashok-leyland|title=Circuit from Ashok Leyland – Commercial Vehicle Magazine in India – Upcoming Truck, Trailer, Tractor & Buses|date=14 December 2016|access-date=31 July 2018}} The bus will be introduced under the National Electric Mobility Plan with an aim of 20% penetration of electric or hybrid vehicles by 2020.{{cite news|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/news/commercial-vehicle/ashok-leyland-unveils-indias-first-indigenous-electric-bus/articleshow/54894000.cms|title=Ashok Leyland unveils India's first indigenous electric bus|first=Shilpa|last=Elizabeth|date=20 October 2016|access-date=31 July 2018|newspaper=The Economic Times}} ===Euro VI Truck=== AT the Delhi Auto Expo 2016, the company showcased its first indigenously produced [[Euro VI]] truck 4940. The truck is powered by the company's flagship range of engine, Neptune, which is an 8l engine that produces 400 hp and 1600Nm of torque. The truck is designed to meet Euro VI norms.{{cite web|url=http://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/ashok-leyland-products-auto-expo-10349|title=Ashok Leyland shows four new products at Auto Expo|website=autocarpro.in|access-date=31 July 2018}} ===iEGR=== In 2017, the company showcased iEGR (intelligent [[exhaust gas recirculation]]) technology for its trucks and buses to meet BS-IV emission standards. The technology also promises other advantages like better fuel efficiency than BS-III trucks, and power transmission up to 400 HP.[http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/ashok-leyland-showcases-tech-to-upgrade-vehicles-to-meet-bsiv-fuel-norms/article9657209.ece Ashok Leyland showcases tech to upgrade vehicles to meet BS-IV fuel norms]. ''The Hindu BusinessLine'' (21 April 2017). Retrieved on 25 December 2018. ===iBUS=== Ashok Leyland announced iBUS in the beginning of 2008, as part of the future for the country's increasingly traffic-clogged major cities. Its Rs 6-million iBus is a feature-filled, low-floor concept bus for the metros revealed during the Auto Expo 2008 in India. This low-floored iBus will have the first of its kind features, including anti-lock braking system, electronic engine management and passenger infotainment. The executive class has an airline-like ambiance with wide LCD screens, reading lights, audio speakers and, for the first time, Internet on the move. A GPS system enables vehicle tracking and display of dynamic route information on LCD screens, which can also support infotainment packages including live data and news. The bus will probably be equipped with an engine from the new Neptune family, which Ashok Leyland also introduced at this exhibition, which is ready for the BS4/Euro 4 emission regulations and can be upgraded to Euro 5.{{cite web|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/News/auto/Rs-60-lakh-iBus-from-Ashok-Leyland/268361/Article1-268357.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100405220529/http://www.hindustantimes.com/News/auto/Rs-60-lakh-iBus-from-Ashok-Leyland/268361/Article1-268357.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 April Ashok Leyland Limited is an Indian multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Chennai and owned by the Hinduja Group. Founded in 1948 as Ashok Motors, it as renamed Ashok Leyland in 1955 following a collaboration with British Leyland. Today it is the second-largest manufacturer of commercial vehicles in India (holding a 32.1% market share as of 2016), the third-largest bus manufacturer, and the tenth-largest manufacturer of lorries.
While its corporate office is located in Chennai, the company operates manufacturing facilities in Ennore, Bhandara, Vijayawada, Hosur, Alwar, and Pantnagar. Ashok Leyland also has overseas manufacturing units in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates, and Leeds, United Kingdom. Additionally, it has a joint venture with the Alteams Group to manufacture high-press die-casting extruded aluminium components for the automotive and telecommunications sectors. The company also makes spare parts and engines for industrial and marine applications.
Ashok Leyland's products range from 1-tonne Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) to 55-tonne Gross Trailer Weight (GTW). This includes trucks, buses ranging from 9 to 80 seats, vehicles for defence and special applications, and diesel engines for industrial, genset, and marine applications. In 2019, the company claimed to be ranked in the top 10 global commercial vehicle makers. It sold approximately 140,000 vehicles (M&HCV and LCV) in 2016. The company has passenger transportation options ranging from 10 seaters to 74 seaters (M&HCV = LCV). In the trucks segment, Ashok Leyland primarily concentrates on the 16 to 25-tonne range and has a presence in the 7.5 to 49 tonne range.
